newsitem.title: USA: CHRYSLER SETS 1998 PRICES LOWER BY 0.6 PCT.
newsitem.headline: CHRYSLER SETS 1998 PRICES LOWER BY 0.6 PCT.

text.p: Chrysler Corp said Wednesday that suggested prices on its 1998 cars and trucks will be an average of 0.6 percent lower than on comparably equipped 1997 models.

"This pricing reflects the realities of a competitive marketplace, but more important, it represents Chrysler's continuing success at cutting costs and finding efficiencies that let us deliver tremendous value to our customers," said James Holden, executive vice president - sales and marketing, in a news release.

"On some vehicles, base prices will be lower. On others, base prices will rise slightly -- in some cases to reflect previously optional features that have been made standard to better match what our customers' orders are telling us they want," Holden said. "There also are changes in the content and prices of certain option packages -- again, to reflect the preferences of buyers."

On a sales weighted average, suggested prices for 1998 Chrysler passenger cars will be 1.3 percent lower than prices on comparably equipped 1997 models. Prices on trucks, including minivans and Jeep vehicles, reflect an average decline of 0.4 percent. Destination charges are unchanged.
The prices announced today do not include vehicles that will be launched later this year, such as the 1998 Dodge Intrepid, Chrysler Concorde, Dodge Durango, and Dodge Ram Van and Wagon.

For example, a Dodge and Plymouth Neon "Highline" is now an entry-level vehicle. With available air conditioning and automatic transmission, the price for a four-door typically equipped Neon Highline model, including destination, is $13,455. The suggested price on a comparably equipped 1997 model was $13,770.
